attackPaths.title: Potential Command Injection

links.basis: finding.route + handler starts before the source in the same file

attackPaths.evidence: Tainted HTTP input reaches exec through a template literal command.

riskMetrics.impactReason: User input reaches an OS command (remote command execution).
riskMetrics.exposureReason: Input comes from an HTTP request on a resolved Express route.

attackPaths.title: Potential Dangerous Code Execution

links.basis: finding.route + handler starts before the source in the same file

attackPaths.evidence: Tainted HTTP input reaches eval as executable code.

riskMetrics.impactReason: User input is executed as JavaScript on the server (remote code execution).
riskMetrics.exposureReason: Input comes from an HTTP request on a resolved Express route.

attackPaths.title: Potential SQL Injection

links.basis: finding.route + handler starts before the source in the same file

attackPaths.evidence: Tainted HTTP input reaches a database query through string concatenation.

riskMetrics.impactReason: User input changes a database query (data read/modify), not direct server execution.
riskMetrics.exposureReason: Input comes from an HTTP request on a resolved Express route.

primary.label: exec
primary.recommendation: At controllers/userController.js:21 (exec): Do not pass user input to a shell. Use execFile/spawn with a fixed command and an argument array, and allowlist the accepted values.

plan.label: exec
plan.recommendation: At controllers/userController.js:21 (exec): Do not pass user input to a shell. Use execFile/spawn with a fixed command and an argument array, and allowlist the accepted values.

plan.label: eval
plan.recommendation: At controllers/userController.js:27 (eval): Remove eval/Function on user input. Parse data with JSON.parse, or map the input to an allowlist of predefined operations.

plan.label: db.query
plan.recommendation: At controllers/userController.js:14 (db.query): Use a parameterized query (bind user values as parameters, e.g. db.query("... WHERE id = ?", [id])) instead of building SQL with concatenation or template literals.
